{
  "participants": [
    {
      "login": "winterrdog",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Approach ACK, but noted signed char bug in socket path sanitization and asked about duplicate binds and abstract socket support"
    },
    {
      "login": "b-l-u-e",
      "stance": "objection",
      "note": "Concept ACK, but reported socket takeover on collision and a Host header regression in bitcoin-cli"
    }
  ],
  "claims": [
    {
      "id": "c:5993254913",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "A second node started with the same -rpcbind=unix:<path> will overwrite the live socket file without error, making the first node unreachable while it remains running.",
      "quote": "second node can take over a live rpc unix socket path, if two nodes use different datadirs but the same -rpcbind=unix:<path> the second node starts with no error..since it removes the first node socke",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author pushed changes adopting ipcbind parameter format to make sockets datadir-scoped by default",
      "author_replies": ["c:6062694537"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:6062694537",
      "status_by_quote": "This should also adderss @b-l-u-e concern about multiple processes messing with each others sockets."
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5999886903",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "bitcoin-cli sends the resolved IP in the HTTP Host header instead of the hostname passed via -rpcconnect=, introducing a behavior change/regression from master.",
      "quote": "the host header contains the resolved IP instead of the hostname given in `-rpcconnect=localhost`",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "fixed",
      "status_note": "author pushed fix for Host header in bitcoin-cli",
      "author_replies": ["c:6062694537"],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": true,
      "status_by_id": "c:6062694537",
      "status_by_quote": "fix `\"Host:` header in bitcoin-cli (@b-l-u-e)"
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4239802579",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "objection",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "On platforms where char is signed, non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes wrap to negative values and match c < 0x20, causing valid UTF-8 paths like /tmp/josé.sock to be replaced with \"unix\" in logs.",
      "quote": "char is signed on some platforms (e.g. x86), so bytes above 0x7f are interpreted as negative values (they wrap around) and also match c < 0x20. this means a utf-8 path like /tmp/josé.sock could end up being replaced with \"unix\" in the logs",
      "clears_with": "change",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4276497992",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "approach",
      "text": "Place Unix socket handling code behind an #ifdef HAVE_SOCKADDR_UN guard to avoid compiling unused code on unsupported platforms.",
      "quote": "why don't we just put this behind an #ifdef HAVE_SOCKADDR_UN guard so we skip this code entirely on platforms that do not support unix sockets ?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4286800301",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "interface",
      "text": "Log host instead of strRPCBind in the bind failure warning to avoid redundant port strings when a port is included in the address.",
      "quote": "strRPCBind can show up in the logs if the optional port is included in the bind address (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8332), leading to logs like this one: Could not bind RPC on address 127.0.0.1:8332 port 8332: Address lookup failed.",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4287174385",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "correctness",
      "text": "Whether duplicate -rpcbind unix socket endpoints unlinking the earlier socket and rebinding silently without warning is intended behavior or should fail like TCP.",
      "quote": "if two -rpcbind values resolve to the same path (e.g. -rpcbind=unix and -rpcbind=unix:http.sock, or the same value in bitcoin.conf and perhaps on the command line), PreparePath() (later called in HTTPServer::BindAndStartListening) removes the first socket file before the second bind(). therefore, both binds succeed without sending a warning is this intentional, or just not something we need to worry about?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "rc:4292770911",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Refactor GetBindAddresses() to reduce cognitive load and streamline the control flow.",
      "quote": "while reviewing GetBindAddresses(), i ended up rewriting it to lower the cognitive load a bit and help me get my head around the flow. thought i could share it and see what you think",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5478881949",
      "part": 1,
      "type": "question",
      "kind": "scope",
      "text": "Whether abstract namespace unix sockets should be supported in the future for Linux-specific setups.",
      "quote": "i saw UnixSocketAddr::SetSockAddr() handles empty and abstract namespace addresses, but we do not support binding or connecting to abstract sockets. do you think it is worth supporting them in the future for linux-specific setups ?",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5478881949",
      "part": 2,
      "type": "suggestion",
      "kind": "maintenance",
      "text": "Update the PR description to match the code regarding Unix socket path resolution.",
      "quote": "the docs, release notes and -help text already match the code, so i think the PR description just needs updating to reflect this, so other reviewers do not get tripped up by the mismatch",
      "clears_with": "answer",
      "status": "open",
      "status_note": "",
      "author_replies": [],
      "other_replies": [],
      "fix_pushed": false,
      "status_by_id": "",
      "status_by_quote": ""
    }
  ],
  "support": [
    {
      "id": "r:5408186323",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "users of other projects relying on Core have wanted Unix domain socket support, and previous libevent blockers are gone",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "c:5993254913",
      "verdict": "Concept ACK",
      "reason": "",
      "substantive": false,
      "evidence": "none",
      "areas": []
    },
    {
      "id": "r:5478881949",
      "verdict": "Approach ACK",
      "reason": "convinced by the implementation and design choices, particularly using std::variant over polymorphism for SocketAddr; security is tight",
      "substantive": true,
      "evidence": "read",
      "areas": ["SocketAddr", "UnixSocketAddr::SetSockAddr()"]
    }
  ],
  "notes": "winterrdog reviewed the C++ implementation and gave an Approach ACK, but noted a signed char bug when sanitizing UTF-8 socket paths for logging, asked about duplicate bind handling and abstract socket support, and suggested refactoring GetBindAddresses().",
  "waiting_on": [
    {
      "on": "author",
      "what": "address winterrdog's review findings including signed char path sanitization bug, duplicate bind question, and refactoring suggestion",
      "id": "r:5478881949"
    }
  ]
}
